Made this notebook to check that I get the same results as Gallagher et al on their parameter estiamtes directly. After that, we investigate if median stan draws line up with their estimates.\

But AT scores look exactly right using the python functions, so I'm assuming that I can compare this metric against a Stan model that gets the other ones right. Also looks right against Figure 1 in article.

eMMDs and eTTP look way off in python and this needs to be resolved.

## Check against Stan

We now fit the same parameters using Stan to see if any future discrepancies are due different parameter estimations being wildly different for Bayesian techniques.

According to the supplemental S2.3 the fitted vals were.:

"For this reason, the parameters rS and R0 are set to values from the literature quoted in Table S2, while the cost of resistance if given a default value of 1−rR/rS = 0.1 ... Furthermore, to ensure the identifiability of the model in this reduced information context, we also exclude the initial tumor density N0 from the parameter fitting; instead, this is set equal to the first recorded PSA measurement (normalized relative to the maximal PSA value recorded). We therefore *only fit the turnover (defined as d/rS) and K*"

**fixed** rS = 0.027 rFrac = 0.00001 R0 = 0.00001 \* n0 - first cycle param csv says 0.0001, where as table 2 in supplemental says 0.001 cost = 0.1 dD = 1.5 n0 - first measurement, and since it the data is normalized by first measurement, this is always 1.

**estimated** turnover K free Sigma - since we need to assume a noise model

```{r}
ids <- c(12,20,25,78,85)
fixed_vals <- c(rS=0.027, rFrac = 0.00001, cost = 0.1, dD = 1.5, n0 = 1)

fits <- list()
for (id in ids){
  stan_data <- make_stan_data(id, first_cycle = T, make_priors(), fixed_vals = fixed_vals, prior_only = 0, run_diagnostics=0) 
  model <- cmdstan_model(here("stan/model_switchable.stan"))
  fit <- model$sample(data = stan_data, chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, refresh = 100, init = 2)
  fits <- append(fits, fit)
}

stan_data <- make_stan_data(id, first_cycle = T, make_priors(), fixed_vals = fixed_vals, prior_only = 1, run_diagnostics=0) 
pror_model <- cmdstan_model(here("stan/model_switchable.stan"))
prior_fit <- model$sample(data = stan_data, chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, refresh = 100, init = 2)
```

```{r}
ids <- c(12, 20, 25, 78, 85)
fixed_vals <- c(rS = 0.027, rFrac = 0.00001, cost = 0.1, dD = 1.5, n0 = 1)
model <- cmdstan_model(here("stan/model_switchable.stan"))

fits <- list()
for (id in ids) {
  stan_data <- make_stan_data(id, first_cycle = TRUE, make_priors(), fixed_vals = fixed_vals)
  fits[[as.character(id)]] <- model$sample(data = stan_data, chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, init = 2)
}
# priors don't depend on patient data, so one prior-only run covers every patient
prior_fit <- model$sample(data = modifyList(stan_data, list(prior_only = 1)),
                          chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, init = 2)

```

```{r}
get_at_draws <- function(fit, kappa = .2) {
  spread_draws(fit$draws(), turnover, K, cost, rR, dR, n0, rFrac) |>
    mutate(AT_score     = calc_delta_benefit(kappa = kappa, dR = dR, K = K, rR = rR, R0 = rFrac * n0),
           can_progress = progression_possible(cost, turnover, n0, K))
}

at_draws <- map_dfr(fits, get_at_draws, .id = "PatientId") |>
  mutate(PatientId = as.integer(PatientId))
prior_at <- get_at_draws(prior_fit)

count(at_draws, PatientId, can_progress)   # how much each patient loses to the filter

at_draws <- filter(at_draws, can_progress)   # prior is left unfiltered

paper_at <- param_df |>
  filter(PatientId %in% ids) |>
  mutate(AT_score = calc_delta_benefit(kappa = .2, dR = dR, K = K, rR = rR, R0 = R0))
at_medians <- at_draws |> group_by(PatientId) |> median_qi(AT_score)

ggplot(at_draws, aes(AT_score)) +
  # no PatientId, so it shows in every panel. Unfiltered prior has AT scores in the thousands, so only draws inside the plotted window go into the density
  geom_density(data = prior_at, aes(x=AT_score))+
  geom_density(fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = .5, colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(data = at_medians, aes(xintercept = AT_score)) +
  geom_vline(data = paper_at, aes(xintercept = AT_score), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ PatientId, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 10)) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r}
ggplot(at_draws, aes(K)) +
  geom_density(data = select(prior_at, K), fill = "grey80", colour = NA) +  # no PatientId, so it shows in every panel
  geom_density(fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = .5, colour = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~ PatientId, scales = "free_y") +

ggplot(at_draws, aes(turnover)) +

  geom_density(fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = .5, colour = NA) +
```
